items.title: US states sue popular kitmaker TP-Link over China risks
items.summary:
Several U.S. states filed a lawsuit against TP‑Link, alleging the company misled customers about security and reliance on Chinese suppliers.
The case focuses on supply‑chain risk.

items.title: FBI, French authorities seize deepfake CSAM-for-sale websites
items.summary:
FBI and French authorities seized websites selling deepfake child sexual abuse material.
The sites featured content from social media platforms.

items.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
items.summary:
SonicWall released hotfixes for four vulnerabilities in SMA1000 gateways.
The most severe flaw allows unauthenticated SSRF to reach internal functions.
No evidence of exploitation has been reported.

items.title: Poetry is the new AI security threat as PoeLLM malware infects 3K+ servers
items.summary:
PoeLLM malware uses poetic code to infect over 3,000 AI servers, turning them into crypto miners.
The campaign, named Canto Incognito, targets exposed LLM infrastructure.

items.title: Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November
items.summary:
Microsoft will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments in Outlook Web and the Windows client starting November.
The change aims to reduce malware distribution via these file types.

items.title: Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely
items.summary:
LMCache, a caching layer for LLM servers, has a critical flaw that permits unauthenticated remote code execution via ZeroMQ.
No patch is currently available.

items.title: PoeLLM Malware Infects 3,400+ Servers to Expand Crypto Mining Botnet
items.summary:
Researchers found PoeLLM malware on more than 3,400 servers, installing cryptocurrency miners.
The operation is called Canto Incognito.

items.title: PoeLLM malware infects exposed AI servers in cryptomining attacks
items.summary: PoeLLM malware targets exposed AI services, converting compromised servers into scanners and launchpads for crypto mining.

items.title: PoeLLM malware has assembled a sweeping botnet, taking technical cues from a poem
items.summary: PoeLLM malware has built a botnet of over 3,400 servers, using poetic coordinates to hide its infrastructure.

items.title: Oklahoma judge’s Flock ruling shows the power of Supreme Court’s digital evidence decision
items.summary: A federal judge dismissed Flock camera evidence in a drug trafficking case after a Supreme Court ruling on geofencing, underscoring the influence of digital evidence decisions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Exploitation attempts against critical Atlassian flaw have begun (CVE-2026-21589)
items.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 arbitrary file access vulnerability in Data Center products shortly after patch release.

items.title: Georgia Power, Alabama Power Data Breach Hits 400,000 Accounts
items.summary: Southern Company notified customers that hackers accessed utility account information, affecting 400,000 accounts across Georgia Power and Alabama Power.

items.title: OT Coalition Urges CISA to Mandate Federal OT Security
items.summary: OT Coalition urges CISA to enforce baseline security standards for federal operational technology, emphasizing the need for mandatory OT security measures.

items.title: Cyber experts call on CISA to create mandatory federal OT rules
items.summary: Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition releases a white paper urging CISA to establish mandatory federal OT rules, setting baseline security requirements for critical infrastructure control systems.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ransomware has a new target. Is your backup ready?
items.summary: Ransomware groups increasingly target backup systems to eliminate recovery options, and Kaseya stresses the importance of isolated, immutable, and regularly tested backups that attackers cannot reach.

items.title: Gremlin Foresight AI finds system weaknesses and verifies the fixes
items.summary: Gremlin announces general availability of Gremlin Foresight AI, which identifies reliability risks before incidents and helps engineering teams accelerate development while maintaining mission‑critical resilience.

items.title: Imply Lumi connects SIEM tools and AI agents to more security data
items.summary: Imply launches Imply Lumi, a data platform for agentic SIEMs that integrates SIEM tools with AI agents, aiming to manage growing data volumes and support AI‑driven investigations while preserving existing workflows.

items.title: Qilin Ransomware Suspect Arrested in Japan, Extradited to Germany
items.summary: Japanese authorities arrest a suspect linked to Qilin ransomware and extradite him to Germany for hacking charges, highlighting international cooperation in cybercrime investigations.

items.title: FortiBleed is still active, with attackers locking admins out of Fortinet firewalls
items.summary: FortiBleed campaign continues, with attackers locking out administrators of Fortinet firewalls; FBI and Secret Service advisory reports over 86,000 compromised devices across 194 countries.

items.title: Vijil DART tests AI agents for security flaws and policy violations
items.summary: Vijil releases Diamond Adaptive Red Teaming for Agents (DART), an automated system that probes AI agents for security flaws and policy violations using adversarial agents that learn and adapt across multiple attack turns.

items.title: Edgescan Atomic validates attack paths with controlled AI testing
items.summary: Edgescan launches Edgescan Atomic, an autonomous penetration‑testing tool built on agentic AI that can run alongside Edgescan’s continuous security platform or as a standalone solution to validate AI‑powered attack paths.

items.title: Trustero automates vendor document reviews with human approval
items.summary: Trustero introduces Trustero Third‑Party Risk Management (TPRM), automating vendor document reviews with AI and human approval to streamline vendor risk management by recommending risk determinations.

items.title: Attackers Hide AI Prompt Injections Inside Phishing Emails
items.summary: Barracuda identified phishing emails that embed AI prompt injections designed to manipulate both human users and AI assistants.

items.title: Hackers exploit critical Atlassian flaw after public PoC release
items.summary: Atlassian disclosed CVE‑2026‑21589, a critical unauthenticated file‑access vulnerability affecting Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, and other products. Attackers are exploiting it without authentication, and Atlassian rated it CVSS 9.3.

items.title: Advantest Discloses Data Breach Months After Ransomware Attack
items.summary: Advantest, a Japanese chip‑testing company, reported that personal data was stolen from its servers months after a February 2026 ransomware attack. The breach was disclosed in a SecurityWeek article.

items.title: CVE-2026-21589: Critical unauthenticated arbitrary file access in Atlassian products
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑21589 is a critical arbitrary file‑access flaw in eight Atlassian Data Center products, including Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, and Fisheye. Atlassian assigned it a CVSS score of 9.3.

items.title: The Sixth Voice of the CISO Data Shows Cyber Risk Has Moved Inside the Workflow
items.summary: The 2026 CISO survey shows cyber risk is increasingly embedded in day‑to‑day workflows, with resilience, AI governance, human risk, and board oversight converging within operational systems.

items.title: Telegram Account Behind ASOS Rogue Notification Tied to Gaming Trading
items.summary: Group‑IB research found a Telegram account linked to a fraudulent ASOS customer notification was involved in gaming‑item trading.

items.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials
items.summary: The FBI and Secret Service warned that the FortiBleed credential‑harvesting campaign targeting Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active, exploiting reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA‑256 storage.

items.title: Atlassian Data Center Flaw Draws Exploitation Attempts Within Two Hours of Public Details
items.summary: Within two hours of public disclosure, threat actors began exploiting Atlassian Data Center's CVE‑2026‑21589 flaw, allowing access to sensitive files in products such as Bitbucket, Confluence, and Jira.

items.title: What Is Agentic Pentesting? What It Proves, and Where It Stops.
items.summary: Agentic pentesting solutions claim to autonomously discover, validate, and exploit attack paths like a real attacker. Evaluators should test these claims by assessing the solution's actual capabilities and limits.

items.title: Hackers hijack three country-code domain registries, obtain HTTPS certificates for Google domains
items.summary: Attackers compromised the operators of Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl), and American Samoa (.as) country‑code domains, using the access to issue HTTPS certificates for Google and other large organization domains.

items.title: Apple’s Verified Photography System
items.summary: Apple released Reference Image, a system that verifies an image was taken by an iPhone without linking it to a specific device or photographer, and can confirm multiple images originate from the same iPhone.

items.title: FortiBleed still a bleeding nuisance as FBI confirms ongoing attacks
items.summary:
FBI confirms FortiBleed attacks are ongoing,
affecting tens of thousands of victims and involving multiple ransomware groups.

items.title: Chrome 155 Update Patches 247 Vulnerabilities
items.summary:
Chrome 155 released,
patching 247 vulnerabilities including four critical use‑after‑free bugs in Chromecast, Browser, Navigation, and Track.

items.title: The ASOS incident: When attackers use the channels customers trust
items.summary:
ASOS customers received a malicious push notification claiming a Snowflake breach;
the retailer confirmed an unauthorized message sent via its app and is investigating third‑party activity.

items.title: SonicWall fixes pre-auth SSRF flaw in SMA 1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255)
items.summary:
SonicWall patched four vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 series,
including CVE‑2026‑102255 that could allow unauthenticated attackers to trigger internal requests and perform unauthorized operations.

items.title: Musician sent to prison for $10 million streaming fraud using AI bots
items.summary: A North Carolina musician was sentenced to 18 months for orchestrating a $10 million streaming royalty fraud using AI bots across major music platforms.

items.title: Advantest confirms personal information stolen in ransomware attack
items.summary: Advantest notified affected individuals that a ransomware attack earlier this year exposed personally identifiable data.

items.title: Your Windows PC can now reach other PCs through Windows App
items.summary:
Microsoft made remote PC connections generally available via Windows App,
consolidating access to physical, virtual, and cloud Windows PCs and replacing the separate Remote Desktop app.

items.title: Half of Cybersecurity Pros Still Rely on Passwords Despite Security Concerns
items.summary:
A Yubico survey shows 50% of cybersecurity professionals still rely on passwords,
highlighting a gap between security awareness and adoption of secure authentication methods in enterprises.

items.title: Anthropic Introduces 3-Tier Cyber Verification Program for AI Access
items.summary:
Anthropic launched a three‑tier Cyber Verification Program combining CVP and Project Glasswing,
offering graded access to its advanced AI models.

items.title: One breach, please, and make no mistakes
items.summary:
The article discusses autonomous AI agents attacking public infrastructure
and stresses the need for preparation to mitigate agentic threats during real incidents.

items.title: ASOS Confirms Cyberattack, Data Breach
items.summary: ASOS confirmed a cyberattack after hackers compromised a third‑party communication platform and sent rogue notifications to users, indicating a data breach.

items.title: ASOS confirms data breach after “hacked” app alert reaches shoppers
items.summary: UK retailer ASOS confirmed a data breach after a notification claiming a hack was sent to shoppers via its app at about 10 am on 6 October 2026; the company serves 16.5 million active customers worldwide.

items.title: Pwn2Own Hackers Find 32 Zero-Day Vulnerabilities on Day One
items.summary: Ethical hackers at Pwn2Own Ireland discovered 32 zero‑day vulnerabilities across multiple products on the first day of the event, as announced by the organizers.

items.title: Anthropic loosens Claude’s cyber restrictions for verified defenders
items.summary: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program, granting vetted security professionals access to Claude with fewer automated blocks for tasks such as malware analysis, and introduced three tiers based on the scope of cybersecurity work.

items.title: Inside a brand deal scam targeting YouTube creators
items.summary: A scam uses plausible sponsorship offers to impersonate Google accounts and compromise YouTube creators’ accounts by tricking them into revealing credentials.

items.title: Danish CPR Breach Highlights Challenge of Supply Chain Risk
items.summary: A breach of the Danish Central Register of Persons exposed data of 8.8 million citizens through third‑party access, highlighting supply chain risk.

items.title: Anthropic Expands Claude Access for Vetted Cyber Teams as Glasswing Finds 129,000 Flaws
items.summary: Anthropic broadened its program for vetted cybersecurity teams, allowing reduced safeguards when testing its AI models; Project Glasswing reported 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.

items.title: Wikimedia Says Rogue OpenAI Agents Tried to Turn Its Tools Into Proxies
items.summary: Wikimedia investigated activity where rogue OpenAI agents attempted to use its tools as proxies, as reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: 100+ Compromised Websites Use Fake Cloudflare Checks to Deliver LunexStealer
items.summary: CERT‑UA identified more than 100 compromised websites that injected malicious JavaScript to deliver LunexStealer, linked to threat cluster UAC‑0277.

items.title: Atlassian Patches Critical Vulnerability Affecting 8 Products
items.summary: Atlassian released patches for a critical vulnerability that enabled unauthenticated attackers to access files in the web application root directory, affecting eight of its products.

items.title: AI Agent Gateway: Open-source tool keeps credentials out of agent configs
items.summary: Tuskira’s AI Agent Gateway is an open‑source solution that sits between AI agents and external services, keeping credentials out of agent configurations and running in the user’s own environment without requiring a Tuskira account.

items.title: OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm, so experimental keys need replacing
items.summary: OpenSSH 10.6 adds a post‑quantum signature algorithm, requiring replacement of experimental keys. The release cycle will be accelerated to deliver bug fixes faster, following a surge of security findings identified with AI assistance.

items.title: AI endpoint management: Visibility, compliance, and remediation
items.summary: Endpoint fleets are expanding faster than security teams can manage, driven by hybrid work, cloud adoption, and new CVEs. Manual tracking and remediation are no longer sufficient, and AI‑driven endpoint management can provide visibility, compliance, and automated remediation.

items.title: Even with OT network visibility, critical infrastructure operators struggle with legacy equipment
items.summary: Critical infrastructure operators use an average of seven security tools but still lack full visibility of OT networks. Legacy equipment is the most common visibility gap, cited by 52% of respondents, making it hard to see all assets.

items.title: Automation, AI agents or people? Sorting out who handles each security finding
items.summary: Over half of surveyed senior security leaders anticipate difficulty simplifying software security programs if current practices continue. The main challenge is determining responsibility for addressing scanner findings in large organizations.

items.title: South Korean president calls for creation of tools that stop all cyber-attacks
items.summary: South Korean President urges development of comprehensive tools to prevent all cyber attacks, calling for a complete security paradigm refresh in the AI era.

items.title: Personal Information for Over 1 Million People Stolen in a Cyberattack on Arizona’s Court System
items.summary: A cyberattack on Arizona’s court system exposed personal data for more than one million individuals, including records dating back 30 years. The breach involved the Arizona Supreme Court’s database.

items.title: Beyond asset discovery. Real-life CrowdRecon use case explored
items.summary: CrowdRecon’s use case demonstrates that asset discovery extends beyond listing internet‑facing assets to mapping relationships, assumptions, and potential attack paths that evolve with product changes.

items.title: Anthropic reconfigures its cool kids security program
items.summary: Anthropic has restructured its security initiatives, transforming Project Glasswing and the Cyber Verification Program into a triple‑tier threat‑hunting club.
